name: Cost and time to get licensed, by state and license
description: Exam, application and first-license fees, the required training hours, a time in months only where the owner states one, minimum age and the criminal record policy, for each license and certification DecipherU covers, by state where the board sets its own rules. Only verified fields appear; a blank means not verified, never zero.
cite_as: DecipherU. (2026). Cost and time to get licensed, by state and license [Data set]. https://decipheru.com/data/licensing-costs

fields.months_owner_stated: A duration the owner states, such as a permit holding period or a BLS ceiling. Blank when no owner states one. We do not convert required hours into months; use hours_required.
fields.fees_usd: Exam, application and first-license fees the board or owner lists, in US dollars. Fingerprinting or a credit report is counted only where source_note says so and names the price. Leaves out courses, tuition, state-added fees and renewal.
fields.min_age: Minimum age in years where the board or owner states one.
fields.criminal_record_policy: review (the board decides case by case) or restricted, only where a board page says so. Blank means no rule was verified, not that none exists.
fields.hours_required: Hours of instruction (or supervised work, see hours_kind) the board or owner page states, as a number. Blank when the page gives none or gives a condition. Compared across states only for the same kind.
fields.as_of: The date the entry was last checked against its sources.

funding.name: WIOA training funds (Individual Training Accounts)
funding.who_it_can_help: Adults and laid-off workers who the local workforce board decides it can serve. Local boards, not DecipherU, decide.
funding.what_it_can_pay: Tuition and fees at training programs that are on your state's eligible training provider list. In New York, state policy says a course must be on that list to be paid for with an Individual Training Account.
funding.how_to_start: Find your American Job Center, ask about WIOA training funds, and bring the program you have in mind so staff can check it against the state list.
caveats: Being on the state list does not guarantee money. The New York advisory says funding depends on an assessment of your needs, and the course must train for an occupation the local board names as in demand.
Texas says a program also generally has to match a target occupation on the board's list.
Eligibility is decided by the program, not by DecipherU. Nothing on this page is a promise of approval.

source.name: New York State Department of Labor, Technical Advisory 18-02.7 (2026-02-06)

funding.name: American Job Center
funding.who_it_can_help: Anyone looking for work, training or career help. Veterans get priority referrals to jobs and training, per the Department of Labor.
funding.what_it_can_pay: Nothing directly. It is the front door to WIOA training funds and other help, and it can tell you what applies to you.
funding.how_to_start: Search by location on the CareerOneStop finder, then call before you visit to ask which services that center offers.
caveats: CareerOneStop says to click a center's name to see which services it offers and to ask about the services you want before you visit.
Eligibility is decided by the program, not by DecipherU. Nothing on this page is a promise of approval.

funding.name: Texas: Eligible Training Providers and Workforce Solutions
funding.who_it_can_help: Texas adults and laid-off workers served by one of the local workforce boards.
funding.what_it_can_pay: Individual Training Accounts that boards use to fund training, for programs on the statewide list.
funding.how_to_start: Search the statewide list at the Texas Workforce Commission, then contact your local Workforce Solutions office. Texas has 28 local boards that oversee more than 170 offices.
caveats: TWC says being on the list does not guarantee a board will refer you to a program or that the program will get funds.
Programs other than registered apprenticeships generally must match a target occupation on a board's list.
Eligibility is decided by the program, not by DecipherU. Nothing on this page is a promise of approval.

funding.what_it_can_pay: WIOA training vouchers for courses on the list, per the Department of Labor's policy.
funding.how_to_start: Search by training provider, course offering or apprenticeship on the state site, then visit a New York State Career Center.
caveats: The state site says being on the list does not guarantee that a particular person can enroll with WIOA money, and to contact a New York State Career Center to ask.
Eligibility is decided by the program, not by DecipherU. Nothing on this page is a promise of approval.

source.name: New York State Department of Labor, Eligible Training Provider List

funding.name: New York: Office of Strategic Workforce Development grants
funding.who_it_can_help: Mostly employers and training providers that apply for the grants. A person may benefit by joining a program one of them runs.
funding.what_it_can_pay: The office funds employer-driven workforce training programs. It is not a voucher you apply for as an individual.
funding.how_to_start: Read the office page for current grant rounds, then ask training providers whether they run a funded program.
caveats: This is a grant to programs, not a benefit paid to individuals.
Eligibility is decided by the program, not by DecipherU. Nothing on this page is a promise of approval.

source.name: Empire State Development, Office of Strategic Workforce Development

funding.name: Florida: CareerSource local boards
funding.who_it_can_help: Florida job seekers who want help from a local workforce board.
funding.what_it_can_pay: Local boards run WIOA services in Florida. The state list of approved training programs was not opened this session, so what a board can pay for is not checked yet.
funding.how_to_start: Use the CareerSource Florida local team search, or Employ Florida, and ask the board about training funds and its approved program list.
caveats: The Florida Department of Commerce site that holds the state list blocked our automated reader, so its page is not cited here.
Eligibility is decided by the program, not by DecipherU. Nothing on this page is a promise of approval.

funding.name: GI Bill: licensing and certification tests and prep courses
funding.who_it_can_help: Veterans and others who have GI Bill entitlement.
funding.what_it_can_pay: VA says it repays up to $2,000 per test for a job that requires a license or certification, and that you can use VA education benefits for approved prep courses. The cost comes out of your entitlement.
funding.how_to_start: Use VA's search tool to see whether your test is approved, then follow the repayment steps on the page.
caveats: VA covers only tests approved for the GI Bill. If a test is not listed, VA says it may still be valid but not yet approved.
Eligibility is decided by the program, not by DecipherU. Nothing on this page is a promise of approval.

source.name: VA, Licensing and certification tests and prep courses

funding.name: GI Bill education benefits
funding.who_it_can_help: Service members, veterans and some family members with GI Bill benefits.
funding.what_it_can_pay: VA lists tuition and expenses while training for a job, including for non-college programs and apprenticeships. The amount depends on the benefit and the school.
funding.how_to_start: Use the GI Bill Comparison Tool to check a school or program, then apply for education benefits on VA.gov.
caveats: Each GI Bill benefit has its own rules on service and time limits that VA checks.
Eligibility is decided by the program, not by DecipherU. Nothing on this page is a promise of approval.

funding.name: Veteran Readiness and Employment (VR&E, Chapter 31)
funding.who_it_can_help: Veterans and service members with a service-connected disability that limits their ability to work, per VA.
funding.what_it_can_pay: Employment support and education or training services that a VA counselor decides are needed.
funding.how_to_start: Apply on VA.gov. VA then schedules an evaluation with a Vocational Rehabilitation Counselor.
caveats: VA lists a service-connected disability rating of at least 10 percent and no dishonorable discharge as requirements, and a counselor decides entitlement.
Eligibility is decided by the program, not by DecipherU. Nothing on this page is a promise of approval.

funding.name: Federal Pell Grant
funding.who_it_can_help: Undergraduate students with financial need who have not earned a bachelor's, graduate or professional degree, per Federal Student Aid.
funding.what_it_can_pay: Costs at an eligible school. The maximum for the 2026-27 award year is $7,395. The amount depends on your Student Aid Index, the school's cost of attendance and your enrollment.
funding.how_to_start: Submit the FAFSA. Schools use it to decide whether to offer a grant and how much.
caveats: The program has to be at a school that takes federal aid, so ask the school whether it does for the course you want.
Eligibility is decided by the program, not by DecipherU. Nothing on this page is a promise of approval.

source.name: Federal Student Aid, Federal Pell Grants

funding.name: Workforce Pell Grant (short programs)
funding.who_it_can_help: Students with financial need in a short program that the state governor and the Department of Education have approved. A bachelor's degree does not rule you out, per the Department.
funding.what_it_can_pay: Tuition for approved short-term programs of about 8 to 15 weeks. The Education Department's August 4, 2026 release describes programs of 8 to 15 weeks.
funding.how_to_start: Ask the school whether the specific program is an approved Workforce Pell program, then complete the FAFSA.
caveats: Statutory effective date is July 1, 2026. Schools could apply for program approval starting July 1, 2026, and the first approval was announced August 4, 2026, so few programs may be approved yet.
Each state governor identifies which programs fit in-demand fields, so a program that qualifies in one state may not in another.
Clock-hour limits and the exact outcome benchmarks were not checked yet.
Eligibility is decided by the program, not by DecipherU. Nothing on this page is a promise of approval.

source.name: U.S. Department of Education, final rule press release (2026-05-18)

funding.name: Employer tuition assistance (IRS Section 127)
funding.who_it_can_help: Employees whose employer offers an educational assistance program.
funding.what_it_can_pay: Education costs your employer pays, such as tuition, books, equipment, fees and supplies. The IRS says an employer can exclude up to $5,250 per employee each year from wages under a qualifying program.
funding.how_to_start: Ask your human resources team whether the company has an educational assistance program and what it covers.
caveats: The IRS requires the program to meet Section 127 rules. Whether a company offers one, and what it pays, is up to the company.
Eligibility is decided by the program, not by DecipherU. Nothing on this page is a promise of approval.

source.name: IRS, Publication 15-B (2026), Employer's Tax Guide to Fringe Benefits

funding.name: Lifetime Learning Credit
funding.who_it_can_help: Taxpayers paying for courses to get or improve job skills, with income under the limit.
funding.what_it_can_pay: A credit of up to $2,000 per return, per the IRS. It can lower your tax to zero but the excess is not refunded.
funding.how_to_start: Keep your tuition statement and ask a tax preparer, or read IRS Publication 970, before you file.
caveats: Publication 970 for 2025 lists a phase-out and a limit of $90,000 income for single filers and $180,000 for joint filers. Check the current year's figures.
The school must be an eligible educational institution. Exam fees alone are not tuition.
Eligibility is decided by the program, not by DecipherU. Nothing on this page is a promise of approval.

source.name: IRS, Publication 970 (2025), Tax Benefits for Education

funding.name: SpouseWorks Scholarship (formerly MyCAA)
funding.who_it_can_help: Spouses of active-duty, National Guard and reserve service members under qualifying Title 10 orders, across all ranks, per Military OneSource.
funding.what_it_can_pay: Up to $4,000 toward a license, certification or associate degree, or continuing education to keep a license or certification needed for work.
funding.how_to_start: Create an account on the SpouseWorks site, which checks eligibility, and call Military OneSource to talk to a career coach.
caveats: The program was called MyCAA and still appears under that name in many places.
Eligibility is decided by the program, not by DecipherU. Nothing on this page is a promise of approval.

funding.name: SNAP Employment and Training
funding.who_it_can_help: People who get SNAP benefits, where their state runs a program they can join.
funding.what_it_can_pay: Help finding a job, training for a new career or moving up, with support such as case management, transportation help, childcare, books and supplies, per USDA.
funding.how_to_start: Pick your state on the USDA page to find your state's SNAP Employment and Training program, or ask your SNAP office.
caveats: Every state runs its own program with its own providers and offerings. USDA does not list what any one state pays for on this page.
Eligibility is decided by the program, not by DecipherU. Nothing on this page is a promise of approval.

source.name: USDA Food and Nutrition Administration, SNAP Employment and Training
